info.title: NthCase CLI
info.description: nth — trigger NthCase mobile and web test runs from CI or a script, wait for the verdict, and gate the pipeline on the exit code. Authenticates with an API key from the environment (NTH_API_KEY), never a flag.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: nth — trigger NthCase runs and read results from CI or scripts. Auth: set NTH_API_KEY (env-only).

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --json
options.description: Machine-readable JSON output (the real API DTO shape). [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Extra diagnostics on stderr (never the API key). [default: False]

commands.name: whoami
commands.description: Identify the key's workspace {id, name} — verifies the key + config.

commands.name: scenarios
commands.description: Scenario commands.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List scenarios as a lookup table (id, name, state, source, stepCount, updatedAt).

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show one scenario's full definition, where a run of its plan may fail and what settles each, and what stands between it and a schedule: each action the trust count holds, with its reason.

commands.name: compile
commands.description: Compile a scenario into the plan its runs replay. COSTS CREDITS (a spend), and the new plan replaces what future runs — scheduled ones included — replay by default; pin the current version first with `scenarios set-plan` if something depends on it. Non-blocking without --wait.

options.name: --model
options.description: Optional LLM model override; omit for the workspace default.

options.name: --operation-id
options.description: Optional idempotency key (a guid). The same value returns the SAME compile instead of paying for a second one.

options.name: --wait
options.description: Block until the compile is terminal; exit 0 on Completed, 1 on Failed, 3 on timeout. [default: False]

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Max seconds to wait with --wait (default 600). [default: 600]

commands.name: compile-run
commands.description: Read one compile-run — the authoritative outcome of a compile. Poll it until status is terminal.

arguments.name: SCENARIOID
arguments.description: The scenario the compile belongs to (the one passed to `scenarios compile`).

arguments.name: COMPILERUNID
arguments.description: The compile-run's id, as returned by `scenarios compile`.

commands.name: plans
commands.description: Every compiled plan version, newest first, with the replay pointer. UNTRUSTED prints `unreadable` for a version whose plan could not be read — that is not zero, and the schedule gate refuses on it.

commands.name: set-plan
commands.description: Choose which compiled plan version unnamed runs replay — or clear the choice by omitting --version. Selects among versions that already exist; nothing is recompiled and no step is touched.

options.name: --version
options.description: The compiled plan version to replay, from `scenarios plans` — or omit to CLEAR the pointer and follow the newest again.

commands.name: decisions
commands.description: What the compile pipeline decided about a plan revision — the audit trail for why a step checks what it checks. --json is the full per-action trail.

options.name: --version
options.description: Plan revision to read. Omit for the newest; an unknown one is refused, not substituted.

arguments.name: SCENARIOID
arguments.description: The scenario's id (from `scenarios list` or `scenarios show`).

commands.name: unpin
commands.description: Take a pin off one step: its recorded or pinned selector (or drop end, or the element its check reads) and the record of who put it there. The scenario goes back to DRAFT; compile it again (`scenarios compile`, costs credits) before relying on a run.

options.name: --selector
options.description: The selector (or drag drop end, or check element) that step carries NOW, exactly as `scenarios show --json` prints it. A step that carries something else is refused and nothing changes.

options.name: --slot
options.description: Which of the step's elements: action (its selector), dropEnd (its drag's drop end) or check (the element its check reads). Leave it out to take the one slot carrying --selector; name it when two carry the same value.

arguments.name: STEPORDER
arguments.description: The SCENARIO step's number, as `scenarios show --json` lists it in `order`.

commands.name: baselines
commands.description: Every picture a person approved as this scenario's visual baselines: per step, one per screen, with who approved it and through which door, and the run it came from. --json adds each run's device and the picture's address, which opens for minutes. Approving stays a person's, on the run's page in the app.

commands.name: delete-baseline
commands.description: Delete one approved baseline — one step's picture on one screen. It CANNOT be undone: the next run of that step on that screen asks for its picture to be approved again, on the run's page in the app. The step's other screens keep theirs.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Required: the delete cannot be undone. Without it nothing is deleted. [default: False]

arguments.name: BASELINEID
arguments.description: The baseline's ID, as `scenarios baselines` lists it.

commands.name: create
commands.description: Create a scenario from a JSON definition. The create only ever yields a DRAFT — compile it (`scenarios compile`, costs credits) before it can run, and APPROVING stays human-only.

options.name: --file
options.description: The definition as JSON — a file path, or '-' to read stdin. The SAME CreateAiScenarioDto the MCP create_scenario tool takes: targetId, name, optional description, ordered steps. Field rules (the step-kind vocabulary included) are the SERVER's — read its error rather than guessing.

commands.name: update
commands.description: Edit a scenario from a JSON definition. A change to its name, description or steps RESETS it to DRAFT — it cannot run until compiled again (`scenarios compile`, costs credits); a profile change that is not its language or locale does not.

options.name: --file
options.description: The FULL updated definition as JSON — a file path, or '-' to read stdin. The SAME UpdateAiScenarioDto the MCP update_scenario tool takes: name, optional description, ordered steps.

commands.name: trigger
commands.description: Trigger a run. With --wait it blocks until terminal — the CI command (see exit codes).

options.name: --wait
options.description: Block until terminal; set the exit code from the verdict (Passed=0, Failed=1, Error=2, Cancelled=4, timeout=3). [default: False]

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Max seconds to wait with --wait (default 600). [default: 600]

options.name: --model
options.description: Optional LLM model override.

options.name: --device-spec
options.description: Optional: this run's device (JSON string). An app has no device of its own — omit to let the farm pick any available device the build fits. An app with no build needs one of the workspace's own devices: {"farmDeviceId":"<id>"} from `devices list`.

options.name: --mode
options.description: Optional run mode: 'Assisted' auto-accepts the AI's picks so the run completes for review (unverified); omit for the default (Strict).

commands.name: runs
commands.description: Run commands.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List recent runs (paged).

options.name: --scenario
options.description: Only runs of this scenario id.

options.name: --status
options.description: Only runs in this status (e.g. Running, Passed, Failed).

options.name: --failed
options.description: Only runs that failed. [default: False]

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show one run summary (status, timing, cost).

commands.name: logs
commands.description: Fetch a run's redacted device/server logs.

options.name: --since
options.description: Max log seq already seen (0 = from the start). [default: 0]

commands.name: network
commands.description: Fetch a run's captured network entries (sensitive headers and saved secrets masked), or why there are none.

commands.name: cancel
commands.description: Stop a run. A queued run cancels outright; an executing one needs --force. A run cancelled before its first step starts costs nothing: no step ran, so there is no fee, no token and no device time. A run cancelled once its steps have begun is still charged: the run fee plus tokens and device time already spent. Stopping saves future spend only.

options.name: --force
options.description: Required to cancel a run that is actually executing — it stops a device part-way through a step. [default: False]

commands.name: detail
commands.description: One run WITH its per-step results (status, healing, instruction). --json carries each step's full record.

commands.name: discovery
commands.description: Discovery commands — mapping an app costs tokens and holds a real device.

commands.name: trigger
commands.description: Start a discovery of a target app — COSTS CREDITS and holds a real device for minutes. Budgets are clamped server-side and the response echoes what was AUTHORISED. The map is a CANDIDATE: only a human can accept it as the app's grounding.

options.name: --focus
options.description: Priority areas the crawl should reach FIRST, in plain language. Omit to inherit the target's setting.

options.name: --avoid
options.description: Areas the crawl must NOT touch (e.g. 'logout, delete account'). Omit to inherit the target's setting.

options.name: --max-steps
options.description: Cap on agent steps. Clamped server-side to 1-60 (web clamps further to 12).

options.name: --max-tokens
options.description: Token STOP CONDITION for the discovery pass (clamped 1,000-200,000). It does NOT cap what you are charged — the proposal call is uncapped.

options.name: --max-pages
options.description: Cap on distinct pages/screens. Clamped to 1-75. The cheap lever for a cheaper discovery.

options.name: --model
options.description: Optional LLM model override.

options.name: --operation-id
options.description: Optional idempotency key (a guid): retrying with the SAME guid returns the discovery already started instead of paying for a second one. Without it, every call is a new billable discovery; a value that is not a guid is refused.

options.name: --device-spec
options.description: Optional: this discovery's device (JSON string, same shape trigger takes). Call `devices list` first; omit to let the farm pick any available device the build fits. An app with no build needs one of the workspace's own devices: {"farmDeviceId":"<id>"} from `devices list`.

options.name: --wait
options.description: Block until terminal; exit 0 Completed / 1 Failed / 2 Error / 4 Cancelled / 3 timeout. [default: False]

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Max seconds to wait with --wait (default 900 — provisioning alone can take 300). [default: 900]

commands.name: cancel
commands.description: Stop a discovery and stop it spending — the stop lands within one heartbeat and the device is released. The partial map is kept but can never ground a compile. A cancelled discovery is still billed the price quoted when it started. Stopping saves future spend only. Cancelling one that already finished is a benign race: reported calmly, exit 0.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List discovery runs, newest first — the only way to obtain a discoveryId.

options.name: --target
options.description: Only discoveries of this target (app) id.

options.name: --page
options.description: 1-based page number. [default: 1]

options.name: --page-size
options.description: Items per page (default 20). A larger value is trimmed to 100, not refused. [default: 20]

commands.name: show
commands.description: One discovery's live state — while it runs, the phase line says what it is doing right now.

commands.name: detail
commands.description: The full report (map, costs, stop reason). Element lists are withheld unless --include-elements — the same shaping the MCP tool applies.

options.name: --include-elements
options.description: Include every page's and screen's FULL element list. Off by default because the lists are large — turn it on only when you need the selectors, not to browse. [default: False]

commands.name: logs
commands.description: A discovery's REDACTED device/server logs (delta pages, like `runs logs`).

options.name: --since
options.description: Max log seq already seen (0 = from the start). [default: 0]

options.name: --source
options.description: Narrow to one source: engine (the trace), console, network, or tap.

commands.name: pages
commands.description: The page sources a phone discovery kept (live view on): every screen at first sight and the reads around a way out that did not work, with what a person typed taken out, kept as long as its trace. Without --seq, the list; with it, one page's XML.

options.name: --seq
options.description: One page's number, from the list. The page's XML goes to standard output, whole, and its facts to standard error.

commands.name: schedules
commands.description: Schedule commands — a schedule is an unattended recurring spend.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List schedules. The read half of `schedules create` — check here BEFORE creating one, because a duplicate runs forever on its own cadence.

options.name: --search
options.description: Substring match on the schedule's name.

options.name: --status
options.description: Only schedules in this status (e.g. Active, Paused).

commands.name: show
commands.description: One schedule AND which scenarios it runs (each with state and its pinned plan version). Also the right call after a `schedules create` that timed out — a retry would create a SECOND schedule.

commands.name: preview
commands.description: The next N times a cron + timezone actually fires, computed server-side. Free, creates nothing — the check on the TIMEZONE, not just the cron.

options.name: --count
options.description: How many occurrences to return (default 3). [default: 3]

arguments.name: TZ
arguments.description: IANA timezone id the cron is interpreted in (e.g. "Europe/Istanbul").

commands.name: estimate
commands.description: What a schedule would COST before you create one — advisory, free, read-only. A schedule is an unattended recurring spend; this is the price tag.

options.name: --model
options.description: Optional model id; omitted = the workspace default.

options.name: --cron
options.description: Optional cron — supply WITH --tz for the per-month figure.

options.name: --tz
options.description: Optional IANA timezone — supply WITH --cron for the per-month figure.

arguments.name: SCENARIOIDS
arguments.description: Comma-separated scenario ids the schedule would run.

commands.name: create
commands.description: Create a recurring schedule — an UNATTENDED RECURRING SPEND that keeps firing with nobody watching. Check `schedules list` FIRST: a duplicate runs forever on its own cadence. There is NO operation id — a timed-out create that is retried makes a SECOND schedule; recover with `schedules list` or `schedules show`, never a retry. Every member must be Ready and fully trusted or the create is refused.

options.name: --name
options.description: The schedule's name.

options.name: --cron
options.description: The cron expression, 5-field.

options.name: --tz
options.description: IANA timezone the cron is interpreted in.

options.name: --scenarios
options.description: Comma-separated scenario ids (every member follows its scenario's plan setting). Use this OR --member.

options.name: --member
options.description: One member as scenarioId[:planVersion] — repeat per member. planVersion pins that member to an exact compiled plan.

options.name: --description
options.description: Optional description.

options.name: --model
options.description: Optional LLM model override.

options.name: --device-spec
options.description: Optional: the device every run takes (JSON string). Omit to let the farm pick any available device each app's build fits. An app with no build needs one of the workspace's own devices: {"farmDeviceId":"<id>"} from `devices list`.

options.name: --auto-pause
options.description: Auto-pause after this many consecutive failed cycles.

commands.name: update
commands.description: Edit a schedule — a FULL REPLACE, not a patch: send the complete definition every time; members are replaced wholesale (an omitted member is REMOVED), and the firing clock is recomputed from now — even a pure rename moves an imminent firing. Enabled/paused state is untouched.

options.name: --name
options.description: The schedule's name.

options.name: --cron
options.description: The cron expression, 5-field.

options.name: --tz
options.description: IANA timezone the cron is interpreted in.

options.name: --scenarios
options.description: Comma-separated scenario ids (every member follows its scenario's plan setting). Use this OR --member.

options.name: --member
options.description: One member as scenarioId[:planVersion] — repeat per member. planVersion pins that member to an exact compiled plan.

options.name: --description
options.description: Optional description.

options.name: --model
options.description: Optional LLM model override.

options.name: --device-spec
options.description: Optional: the device every run takes (JSON string). Omit to let the farm pick any available device each app's build fits. An app with no build needs one of the workspace's own devices: {"farmDeviceId":"<id>"} from `devices list`.

options.name: --auto-pause
options.description: Auto-pause after this many consecutive failed cycles.

commands.name: pause
commands.description: Stop future cron firings (idempotent). No confirmation, deliberately — stopping a recurring spend must not be taxed. A paused schedule is NOT inert: `schedules run-now` still fires it, deliberately. Resume recomputes the next run from now and never fires missed cycles.

commands.name: resume
commands.description: Re-enable a paused schedule. The next run is recomputed FROM NOW — missed cycles are never fired retroactively. A stored cron/timezone that can no longer be evaluated is refused honestly (edit the schedule, then resume). Resuming a running schedule is a calm success.

commands.name: run-now
commands.description: Fire ONE Manual cycle immediately, through the same launcher and billing gates as cron — A SPEND: one billed run per member, each possibly holding a real phone. The price is knowable BEFORE the press: `schedules estimate` answers it — check it first. Works on a PAUSED schedule, deliberately (pausing stops the cron, not an explicit fire). NO idempotency across calls: every call creates a NEW billed cycle — if this times out, check `schedules show` before any retry. Prints the cycle id; no --wait, because a cycle is many runs with many verdicts and has no single terminal state.

commands.name: devices
commands.description: Device discovery.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the farm's leasable devices (optionally filtered by platform).

options.name: --platform
options.description: Only devices on this platform (Android, iOS, Web).

commands.name: provision
commands.description: Ask the farm to BUILD an emulator/simulator matching a spec from `catalog`, when `devices list` shows nothing suitable. SPENDS THE OPERATOR'S MACHINE, NOT MONEY: it boots a real emulator on the host, capped at TWO concurrent emulators per node; not billed. NO idempotency key — if this fails at the transport level, poll `devices provision-status` BEFORE retrying (a blind retry eats the second slot). The provisioned device joins the SHARED pool.

options.name: --platform
options.description: Platform to build: Android or iOS. Web needs no device.

options.name: --os-version
options.description: Optional OS version from `catalog`, e.g. "16".

options.name: --form-factor
options.description: Optional form factor from `catalog`, e.g. "phone".

options.name: --profile
options.description: Optional AVD hardware profile from `catalog`, e.g. "pixel_7".

options.name: --wait
options.description: Block until the device is Ready (exit 0, prints the deviceId) or Failed (exit 1, prints the farm's reason); exit 3 on timeout. [default: False]

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Max seconds to wait with --wait (default 420 — worst-case boot 180 + adb 120 + queue slack). [default: 420]

commands.name: provision-status
commands.description: Poll a provision: Queued / Provisioning / Ready (with the deviceId) / Failed (with the farm's own reason). The read half of `devices provision` — a provision nobody polls is a request nobody reads.

commands.name: catalog
commands.description: The farm's provisionable capability catalog (valid deviceSpec values per platform).

options.name: --platform
options.description: Only the catalog entry for this platform.

commands.name: nodes
commands.description: THIS workspace's connected machines and their health. NOT a device picker (`devices list` is that) — the value is the WHY, in the default output: each platform's outcome with its reason and remedy (an Answered outcome may carry a caveat — a stated blind spot to check by hand, not a failure), every attached-but-unusable device with what to do about it, and the phones the machine has.

commands.name: apps
commands.description: App (target) commands.

commands.name: register
commands.description: Register a NEW app. It is created PENDING and COMPLETELY INERT — it cannot be discovered, compiled, or run until a workspace member confirms ownership in the app UI: open the app from Apps and press Confirm ownership (the attestation endpoint takes no API key, deliberately). A pipeline that registers an app must hand off to a person.

options.name: --file
options.description: The app definition as JSON — a file path, or '-' to read stdin. The SAME RegisterTargetInput the MCP register_target tool takes: name, platform; Web ⇒ baseUrl, Android/iOS ⇒ buildId, buildArtifactUrl OR appPackageId (absolute http(s) URLs only — the server enforces it); optional environment / explorationFocus / explorationAvoid / configJson. An app has no device of its own: a `device` block in a mobile app's configJson is dropped, and the answer says so.

options.name: --build
options.description: An uploaded build's id (from `builds upload`) for the new app to run — instead of buildArtifactUrl.

commands.name: builds
commands.description: The app's uploaded builds, newest first (* marks the one it runs): name, the app id and version the server read from each file, size, and when it was uploaded. A build whose check (--json) lists sealedFindings runs on the platform's own phones sealed: what those findings ask for is switched off before the app first opens and kept off while the session runs, and the phone's apps are checked afterwards against the list taken before (platformPhonesSealed says it in the server's words).

commands.name: update
commands.description: Make an uploaded build the one the app runs ("Use this build"). The server refuses a build of a different app, of the other platform, of another app's, or already removed — in its own words. Only the build changes; the rest of an app is edited on its page.

options.name: --build
options.description: The uploaded build the app runs from now on — an id from `builds upload` or `apps builds`.

commands.name: grounding
commands.description: Which discovery map a compile of this app grounds in: the mode, the pinned pointer, and what they resolve to. READ ONLY — pinning stays human.

commands.name: suggestions
commands.description: The app's AI-PROPOSED scenarios — the review-and-approve queue `scenarios list` deliberately excludes. READ ONLY: approving one stays human.

commands.name: builds
commands.description: Build commands — an app's build as a file from this machine.

commands.name: upload
commands.description: Upload a build from this machine, streamed as it is read. The server's size limit is read first, so a file over it is refused before a byte is sent. Prints the build's id and the app id and version the server read from it; name the id with `apps register --build` or `apps update --build`. A build no app takes is removed within a day.

options.name: --platform
options.description: The platform the build is for: Android or iOS.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: The build file: an Android .apk, an iOS .ipa, or a .zip holding one simulator .app.

commands.name: notices
commands.description: Print the third-party notices: the licences of the open-source code inside nth. Needs no key and sends nothing.
